The reading I chose: *edit every site that states the compile-failure fail-closed rule, whether or not the words `fail-closed`/`deny-all` appear near it* — which is why a widened grep (`no applicable`, `no polic*`, `compiles`, `uncompilable`, `denies everything`) was run over all 8 rather than trusting the original two-token sweep. It returned exactly the two sites edited. `rls.mdx:18` is the one edit beyond the card's letter: it is the first statement of the rule a reader meets, and the page's own correction sits ~160 lines below it, so under the prompt's test — *could a careful reader still come away believing an empty policy set denies everything?* — leaving it would have failed the test on the page that owns the contract.

**ACCEPT** — PR #8029. Reviewed against GitHub, not against the report's self-description.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| path surface (`get_files`) | **2 files**, both `content/docs/permissions/**` (`authorization.mdx`, `rls.mdx`). **Zero `packages/**`** — ruling 1 honoured |
| CI | **27 checks, no failures.** `Check Changeset` green with `skip-changeset`; `ADR maintainer approval` green (no ADR files) |
| draft / base / mergeable | draft, `main`, `clean` |
| closing keywords | first line `Fixes #7811` — correct, this PR is the whole card. Related cards use the safe form: *"#7665 remains open; #7792 remains open"*. No verb form anywhere |
| diff read directly | both patches read in full; the new wording states the narrow condition **and** names the empty case explicitly |

## Three things it found that the card did not

1. **A third null-returning case.** The card described two states (empty set vs all-fail). Reading `RLSCompiler.compileFilter` directly rather than the card's line citation, the dev found `applicable === 0` also returns `null` **without counting toward the deny** — a `check`-only policy seen on the `using` read pass is skipped, so even a *non-empty* policy list can legitimately yield no filter. The card's two-state model would have produced prose that is still subtly wrong.
2. **A second overstatement, in the opposite direction.** `rls.mdx`'s summary bullet said a policy that can't compile "denies everything". That overstates too: one uncompilable policy *alongside* a compilable one is excluded from the OR-union, not a deny. The card named this file only as a "worth checking while you're in there" — it turned out to contain a real second defect.
3. **`rls.mdx`'s contract section was already exact** and is untouched. Correctly distinguishing "already right, leave it" from "wrong, fix it" is the whole job on a card like this.

## The per-file discipline held

All 8 files checked, **6 left with zero diff**, each with a stated verdict and the reason it is correct for its own layer (attachment resolution-failure, identity write guard, delegated-admin, FLS, OWD default, sharing depth). Then a *widened* sweep for restatements of the compile rule specifically (`no applicable`, `no polic*`, `compiles`, `uncompilable`, `denies everything`) across all 8 — returning only the two sites edited. That closes the gap a file-name sweep leaves: the rule could have been restated in prose that matches neither of the original grep terms.

**On the acceptance test I set** — *"could a careful reader still come away believing an empty policy set denies everything"* — the answer is now no in both edited places, because each states the empty case affirmatively rather than merely omitting the wrong claim.

## Contract deviation, recorded not penalised

No `os-dev-report` comment was posted here; the cloud session went IDLE at *"gates run & pass; awaiting CI report"*, i.e. it waited for CI rather than reporting at draft-PR time as the dispatch required. Accepted directly off the PR under the standing report-lost-is-not-review-stalled rule: the PR body **is** a complete report (contract verification, per-file verdicts, real gate output). Same deviation shape as #7353 last term — worth noting it has now happened twice, both times harmlessly, both times because the dev over-waited rather than under-reported.

Marking ready and arming auto-merge. Tracked to MERGED by this seat, with the `closed_by_pull_requests` check on landing.
